ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\cos B = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, $\sin C = \frac{3}{5}$, and $AC=5$, what is the area of $\triangle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $AH\perp BC$,\\
then $AH=AC\sin C=5\times\frac{3}{5}=3$,\\
$\therefore$ $CH=\sqrt{AC^{2}-AH^{2}}=4$,\\
$\because$ $\cos B=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $BH=AH=3$,\\
$\therefore$ $BC=BH+CH=3+4=7$,\\
$\therefore$ $S_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}\times BC\times AH=\frac{1}{2}\times7\times3=\boxed{\frac{21}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and BC is the base; when drawing the altitude from A to BC, the foot H is located between B and C. Reasoning: Draw AH perpendicular to BC. Because AC=5 and sin C=3/5, in right triangle AHC, AH=AC·sin C=5·3/5=3. By the Pythagorean theorem, CH=sqrt(AC^2-AH^2)=sqrt(25-9)=4. Also because cos B=sqrt(2)/2, angle B=45°. In right triangle ABH, angle B is 45°, therefore the two legs are equal, BH=AH=3. Thus BC=BH+CH=3+4=7. The area of the triangle is (1/2)·BC·AH=(1/2)·7·3=21/2.
